skill.name: exploratory-data-analysis
skill.description: Analyze scientific data files across chemistry, genomics, microscopy, spectroscopy, omics, and general formats. It detects file types, extracts metadata, samples data, checks quality, and creates markdown EDA reports.
skill.summary: Detect formats and generate scientific EDA reports with quality checks.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: No prompt-injection text, credential exfiltration, network activity, or hidden command execution was found. Most static alerts are false positives from markdown code spans, scientific terms, and reference documentation. The remaining issues are archive-processing guidance without explicit safeguards and report output that can overwrite a chosen local path.

remediation.issue: Archive processing guidance lacks explicit safety controls.
remediation.suggestion: Document safe archive inspection: list members, reject absolute or parent paths, enforce size limits, and avoid extraction unless requested.

remediation.issue: The analyzer writes reports with normal write mode.
remediation.suggestion: Check for existing output files, require explicit overwrite confirmation, or use exclusive creation for generated reports.

content.value_statement: Scientific files are hard to inspect because each format stores metadata and quality signals differently. This skill detects the format, samples the data, and creates a structured EDA report.
actual_capabilities: Detects extensions and maps files to six scientific format categories.
Reads format reference notes for chemistry, genomics, imaging, spectroscopy, omics, and general data.
Analyzes CSV, TSV, NumPy, JSON, HDF5, FASTA, FASTQ, and common image files.
Summarizes size, path, modified time, shape, data types, missing values, and basic statistics.
Generates markdown reports with format context, findings, and next-step recommendations.
Suggests relevant libraries and analysis approaches for many specialized formats.
limitations: Detailed parsing depends on optional Python libraries being installed.
Many vendor formats are documented but not fully parsed by the included script.
Large files are sampled, so rare issues may be missed.
The skill does not validate scientific conclusions or replace domain review.

use_cases.title: Profile a new instrument export
use_cases.description: Inspect a new scientific file, identify the format, and create a report before deeper analysis.

use_cases.title: Screen sequence files before pipelines
use_cases.description: Check FASTA or FASTQ structure, sequence counts, length patterns, and quality signals before workflow setup.

use_cases.title: Inventory mixed research datasets
use_cases.description: Review files from several domains and summarize formats, libraries, quality risks, and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze One File
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze `data.csv` with the exploratory data analysis skill. Create a markdown report with format details, quality checks, and next steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single scientific data file.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Related Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Run EDA on `sample1.fastq`, `sample2.fastq`, and `metadata.csv`. Summarize common quality issues and major differences.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of related files from one study.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on Format Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect `experiment.h5` for structure, dataset shapes, attributes, missing values, and memory concerns. Recommend safe steps for large data.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of hierarchical or large scientific files.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Analysis Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the relevant references to design an EDA plan for mixed microscopy and omics data. Include libraries, sampling, and report sections.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning before custom analysis across domains.

output_examples.input: A researcher asks to analyze a FASTQ file.
output: The report identifies FASTQ sequence data and notes read count sampling.
It summarizes read lengths, quality score patterns, and recommended quality control steps.
It suggests downstream sequence filtering, alignment, and annotation checks.

output_examples.input: A data engineer provides a CSV experiment table.
output: The report lists columns, inferred data types, missing values, and numeric summaries.
It highlights possible outliers and duplicate rows for review.
It recommends correlation analysis, imputation choices, and visualization options.

output_examples.input: A microscopist provides a multi-page TIFF image.
output: The report identifies image dimensions, mode, frame count, and intensity range.
It notes metadata and quality checks relevant to microscopy workflows.
It recommends segmentation, background correction, and channel review steps.

best_practices: Confirm the file path and desired output location before running the analyzer.
Install only the scientific libraries needed for the target format.
Use sampling and chunking for large files before requesting full statistical summaries.
anti_patterns: Do not run analysis on private data without approval from the data owner.
Do not extract archives unless the user requests it and safe limits are applied.
Do not treat automated EDA findings as final scientific conclusions.

faq.question: Which formats does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers many chemistry, genomics, microscopy, spectroscopy, proteomics, metabolomics, and general scientific formats.

faq.question: Does it create reports?
faq.answer: Yes. It creates markdown EDA reports with file details, analysis results, quality notes, and next-step recommendations.

faq.question: Can it analyze very large files?
faq.answer: Yes, but it should use sampling, chunking, or memory-aware methods to avoid loading too much data.

faq.question: Does it require extra packages?
faq.answer: Some formats require optional Python libraries such as pandas, NumPy, h5py, Pillow, or Biopython.

faq.question: Can it compare multiple files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create individual reports and summarize differences across related files.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive research data?
faq.answer: It works on local files, but users should review paths, outputs, and sharing policies before analysis.
